1#_: Eating vessels. Chochmas Adam wrote general rule 73 law 13: the large cauldrons in which they brew beer — it appears to me they require tevilat kelim; and even though they fix them and attach them to the ground, nevertheless their law is like a vessel and they have no remedy except that one immerse them or pierce in them a large hole that nullifies them from the category of vessel, and afterward a Jewish craftsman repairs them. But according to what I heard, that the beer they brew in them is not fit for drinking at all until they filter it, it is possible that on this basis the world relies that they do not immerse them; nevertheless requires study, for they are no worse than a slaughter knife below seif 5, since it is fit to use for another food — see in his book Binas Adam more on this:
2#_: Glass. See She'eilat Yaavetz vol. 1 siman 67, who wrote that vessels coming from overseas countries called porcelain and similar to glass vessels do not require tevilah, since it is known that their making is from sand and earth, and metal vessels are spoken of in the parashah; and even though they are thinner, we have no concern for this, for glass vessels are thinner than they, and if not for the fact that when they break they can be repaired by melting — for this reason they equated them to metal vessels — they would require tevilah, and these do not have that remedy — see there:
3#_: To immerse them. Chochmas Adam wrote there law 15: one must insert the entire vessel in water at one time so that none of it remains outside the water, even any amount; and if it is large and one cannot immerse it all at once, it appears to me it is forbidden to immerse in halves, similar to immersion of a niddah, and it is not comparable to hag'alah, which is to expel the prohibition — and once he hag'alah part, he has expelled — but here it is because of impurity, and since part of it remains outside the water, impurity returns and spreads through the entire vessel — end of his words:
4#_: In a mikveh or in water. Chochmas Adam wrote there law 19: it appears to me that in a time of pressing need it is permitted to immerse a glass vessel in snow if it is in one place (see below siman 201 seif 30), for its tevilah is certainly d'rabbanan; but not metal vessels, for according to many poskim it is d'oraisa — see there. [And see responsum Machzik Bracha siman 43 s.v. the general principle that emerges, who wrote that he found in Maharil that he testified before his teachers that they forbade immersing vessels in a well because when they clean them it becomes invalid as drawn water, etc. — see there; and see below siman 201 seif 40 in the gloss and what he wrote there s.k. 28]:
5#_: That the vessel be loose. Shach — what he challenged on this (and it is brought in Baer Heitev s.k. 3) — and it appears his view is that here too in tevilat kelim, even though he loosened his hands, the tevilah did not take effect, a decree lest he not loosen; and see Tiferes Moshe, who resolved his difficulty in Turei Zahav, that there regarding tevilah of impurity a decree is appropriate, for if he does not loosen he may come to a severe prohibition with his hands, such as that he may have relations with a niddah or place in a pure terumah vessel and eat it and it carries the death penalty; which is not so here, for even if he uses this vessel afterward he does not eat a prohibition, for what is inside is not forbidden, as Rama wrote at the end of this siman — therefore they did not decree on this — end of his words — see there:
6#_: That it does not require tevilah. See responsum Shev Yaakov siman 31 regarding vessels fixed in an oven from which they take hot water for kneading dough — he inclined to say they do not require tevilah at all, even if they are of metal, and even though sometimes they pour hot tea-water from them; nevertheless we follow the majority of its use — see there:
7#_: The matzah irons. Baer Heitev in the name of Taz and Shach. And see Peri Megadim Orach Chaim siman 491 in Mishbetzot s.k. 26, who wrote in Yiddish that they place matzos on them — even according to Shach tevilah is required (without a blessing), for it is fit for actual food use. And he further wrote: rib eizen that a non-Jew made requires tevilah with a blessing, for they separate bread with it and call out; and rib eizen that a Jew bought from a non-Jew and pierced it requires study — see there further:
8#_: Pepper mill. See She'eilat Yaavetz vol. 8 end of seif 7, who wrote that mills with which they grind light beans from which they make the beverage kave — it appears they are liable for tevilah, for they are preferable to a pepper mill — see there. And it appears that for this tevilah is without a blessing, since cooking is required — see Baer Heitev s.k. 6; and likewise Peri Megadim Orach Chaim siman 491 in Mishbetzot s.k. 26 — see there:
9#_: To cut cards. Baer Heitev; and see Binas Adam, gate Issur VeHeter siman 65 regarding what they practice at large feasts, to borrow coated earthenware vessels and glass vessels from a Jewish shopkeeper; and he wrote that even though Taz and Shach are concerned for the view of Issur VeHeter to immerse without a blessing when the first bought for cards or commerce, nevertheless since Rama did not bring the view of Issur VeHeter at all, and Peri Chadash also disagrees with him — if so, for Shabbat or guests or a large feast where there is concern they may break if immersed and there will be loss, or there is no time, one may rely to use without tevilah, for tevilat kelim of these is only d'rabbanan according to all; and it is possible that Issur VeHeter also did not write thus except regarding metal vessels, for according to many poskim tevilah is d'oraisa, and so one should be stringent with metal vessels, for it is a doubt of d'oraisa — see there. And see responsum Chinuch ben Yomo siman 52, who wrote on this: a Jew who borrows a glass vessel from a Jewish shopkeeper and agrees with him that he will pay him the value of breakages during the meal and the remainder returns to him if he pays for breakages only according to the seller's principal and gives him a fixed sum for the loan — he is considered a renter, and his law is like the law of a borrower who does not require tevilah (and according to Taz one should immerse it without a blessing); but if he pays breakages according to what he profits on it, he is considered a purchase, for borrowing appraises how much it is worth in the market for any person, and therefore he must immerse — see there; and it appears he means with a blessing:
10#_: If he bought it. See responsum Radvaz vol. 2 siman 945, what he wrote on this:
11#_: He immerses it. Peri Chadash wrote: it is reasonable that glass vessels, for which one is not liable to immerse them except d'rabbanan, are a doubt of d'rabbanan and to be lenient; and whoever does not see in the non-Jew's mind that he wishes to sink them does not require tevilah — see there:
12#_: To immerse it without a blessing. Chochmas Adam wrote: it appears to me that a Jew who holds a glass factory where they make glass and has gentile workers, or the reverse, may rely on those who are lenient, and in time of need it is permitted to use without tevilah, for it is a doubt of d'rabbanan. And shopkeepers must warn buyers of glass not to bless on the immersion unless he holds a gentile glass factory and gentile workers — see there:
13#_: Requires tevilah. And accordingly, when he sells cauldrons to a non-Jew orally because of chametz that requires tevilah after Pesach, and therefore it is better not to sell them — Chochmas Adam there law 3. And it is clear to me that I saw thus in responsum Shivat Tzion in the name of his father the gaon, may his memory be blessed, in the order of selling chametz:
14#_: We do not believe a minor. Because tevilat kelim is d'oraisa — Taz; and see Peri Megadim Orach Chaim siman 491 in Mishbetzot s.k. 26, who wrote requires study, that even with glass vessels, which are d'rabbanan, it also appears he is not believed, since he has a presumption of prohibition like siman 127 seif 3 at the end of the gloss. However, with glass, whoever reached thirteen years need not check after bar mitzvah; and with metal vessels one may say he must know he is an adult — end of his words; however one may say that here too with metal vessels one need not know, for here it is lighter than every d'oraisa prohibition, since if he transgressed and used without tevilah what is inside is not forbidden, as Rama wrote at the end of this siman, and as I wrote this reasoning above s.k. 5 in the name of Tiferes Moshe — see there; and see above siman 201 s.k. 7 and investigate:
15#_: And afterward he borrows it from him. See responsum Rashbash siman 468, who hesitated about this leniency, for it is like an evasion and forbidden — see there; and see responsum Sha'agat Aryeh siman 56 and siman 57, who raised that during bein hashemashot of erev Shabbat and erev Yom Tov one does not immerse metal vessels that require tevilah d'oraisa, but glass vessels, which are d'rabbanan, are permitted; but on Shabbat and Yom Tov themselves, even glass vessels one does not immerse, because this tevilah is not for today's need but for weekday need, and it is forbidden — see there:
